rows.title: Canada, Philippines conclude negotiations for free-trade agreement, aiming for 2027
rows.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. met on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila and formally ended negotiations on a Canada-Philippines free trade agreement, with Ottawa aiming to sign the full deal next year. The two countries first discussed a deal in 2015, and Carney and Marcos restarted the talks about a year ago. Canada-Philippines merchandise trade was a modest $3.4 billion in 2025, while Canada's trade with the ASEAN bloc reached $52.3 billion last year, up about a fifth. The agreement is part of Ottawa's push to diversify trade away from the United States amid U.S. tariffs. Pork exporters are watching closely because Manila is considering limits on pork imports.
rows.fact: Carney and Marcos signed a document closing negotiations on the bilateral free trade agreement, with the full deal to be signed next year. Businesses broadly backed the deal during consultations, while civil-society groups raised concerns about the Philippines' record on the environment, labour and human rights.
rows.outlook: Carney expects the deal to help bilateral trade roughly triple by 2035, and analysts in the article say Canada should also build defence, digital-trade and education ties in the region.
rows.why: 미국 관세 압박 속에서 캐나다가 아시아로 교역처를 넓히는 '무역 다변화' 전략이 실제로 어떻게 추진되는지 보여주는 사례이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how Canada is actually putting a trade-diversification strategy into practice, turning toward Asia under pressure from U.S. tariffs.
rows.term_def: A treaty in which countries agree to cut or remove tariffs and other barriers on goods and services they trade with each other.
rows.note: Last-24h government trade-policy action (talks concluded Nov 14 in Manila). CP body read in full; cross-checked with BNN Bloomberg/CTV and AFP via Arab News (AFP says tariffs will go on more than 90% of tariff lines; AFP's ~$2.4B bilateral trade figure differs from CP's $3.4B merchandise figure, CP figure used).

opinion.title: What does Canada have to gain in a new trade deal with the Philippines?
opinion.author: ER Velasco
opinion.summary: The author argues that the Canada-Philippines agreement offers real but modest gains, because bilateral trade starts from a small base of about $3.4 billion, and that official framing tends to overstate them. Agriculture, especially wheat and frozen pork sold to a fast-growing food importer, is the strongest case for the deal, while Canada's supply-managed dairy, poultry and egg sectors want protection. The piece notes Canada's widening trade deficit with the Philippines but sees the bilateral deal as a wedge toward a broader Canada-ASEAN pact. It concludes the deal's value depends on whether it opens real export channels rather than mostly making imports cheaper.
opinion.why: 정부 발표의 '큰 성과'와 실제 경제적 이익 사이의 차이를 비판적으로 따져보는 연습이 되기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It is good practice in critically weighing a government's 'big win' announcement against the actual economic gains.

rows.title: Fed's Jefferson says he is taking his policy cues from inflation
rows.summary: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Friday that the U.S. economy is growing and the job market has steadied, so inflation is now the main thing guiding his view on interest rates, hinting he could back more hikes after the Fed's quarter-point increase in September. In a speech at UC San Diego, he noted that 12-month PCE inflation was 3.6% in September (core 3.1%), well above the Fed's 2% target, with higher energy costs a major cause. He said the AI boom is already pushing up demand and some prices, such as memory and logic chips, through data-center building and rising stock wealth, while its productivity payoff is likely to come gradually. He warned that rapid job losses from AI could raise unemployment, and that interest-rate policy can treat cyclical slumps but not structural job mismatches.
rows.fact: Jefferson, who voted with the 10-2 majority to hold rates steady at the October meeting, said the path of inflation is the more important signal for policy. He gave no specific guidance on the size or timing of the next move, saying decisions depend on the data, the outlook and the balance of risks. He estimated AI's contribution to overall productivity so far has been limited but could become large.
rows.outlook: Jefferson expects AI to raise the economy's productive capacity substantially but gradually, and expects chip shortages to ease as supply catches up over the medium term.
rows.why: AI 붐이 물가와 금리, 일자리에 어떤 영향을 주는지 중앙은행 2인자의 시각으로 이해할 수 있어 미래 진로와 경제를 함께 생각해 볼 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows, through the eyes of the Fed's second-ranking official, how the AI boom affects prices, interest rates and jobs, which links directly to students' future careers.
rows.term_def: How much output a worker or economy produces per hour of work; when it rises, the economy can grow faster without pushing up prices.
rows.note: Last-24h policy item: Fed Vice Chair speech of Nov 13 (PT), checked against the official text on federalreserve.gov (venue, PCE figures, October vote). October retail sales not yet released.

opinion.title: The AI boom has handed the Fed an inflation problem that rate hikes may not fix
opinion.author: Kristin Schwab
opinion.summary: The piece explains how heavy AI investment is pushing up prices: chip costs flow into phones, computers and game consoles, and the buildout adds pressure on labor, goods demand and possibly energy. Former Fed governor Randy Kroszner expects a December rate hike but doubts it would do much to cool AI spending, given how strong enthusiasm for the technology is. EY-Parthenon economist Gregory Daco expects AI to keep adding to inflation for 12 to 24 months, which could justify more hikes next year. The article ties this to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's planned Nov 15 speech on AI and monetary policy.
opinion.why: 금리 인상이라는 전통적 수단이 AI발 물가 상승에는 잘 듣지 않을 수 있다는 점을 통해 통화정책의 한계를 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches the limits of monetary policy by showing why raising interest rates may not work well against AI-driven inflation.

rows.title: Seoul freezes fuel price caps amid Mideast tensions
rows.summary: South Korea's trade and industry ministry left its fuel price caps unchanged for a fifth straight four-week period. For the four weeks from Nov. 14, the most refiners may charge gas stations is 1,784 won per liter for gasoline, 1,773 won for diesel and 1,380 won for kerosene. The caps began in mid-March, when the U.S.-Iran war disrupted oil supply chains, and have stayed at their current level since late June. The ministry noted that Brent crude, at about $96 a barrel on Nov. 12, has fallen below $100 but is still more than $20 above its late-June level, and that higher ocean freight costs also push prices up. The freeze is meant to keep consumer inflation in check, and the government will adjust these emergency measures depending on the Middle East and domestic conditions.
rows.fact: On Nov. 13 the government kept the ceilings on refiners' wholesale gasoline, diesel and kerosene prices unchanged for another four weeks. This is the fifth consecutive freeze, and the caps have been at this level for 20 weeks.
rows.outlook: The ministry said it will adjust the emergency measures as needed while watching Middle East developments and the domestic economy.
rows.why: 정부가 기름값 상한을 정해 물가를 누르는 정책이 우리 생활비와 나라 재정에 어떤 득실을 주는지 이해할 수 있는 좋은 사례이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It is a real example of how a government price ceiling holds down everyday costs but carries hidden trade-offs for public finances and markets.
rows.term_def: A legal maximum price set by the government, here the most refiners may charge gas stations, used to keep prices from rising too fast.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: policy announced Nov 13, 20:31 KST, just outside the 24h window; no qualifying Korean policy/data item found for Nov 14. Figures cross-checked against the Yonhap version in The Korea Herald.

opinion.title: Winter is coming for Korea's flush refiners
opinion.author: Kim Dong-young
opinion.summary: The piece says Korea's four big refiners had a highly profitable year during the Middle East war, with third-quarter refining and lubricant operating profit of 5.9 trillion won, about 4.8 times the year-earlier level, but that windfall is fading as crude supply recovers. It calls the domestic price cap a major unresolved issue: the government has set aside a 4.2 trillion won reserve and proposed about 1.45 trillion won more in next year's budget for fourth-quarter losses. Refiners claim about 5 trillion won in losses and want compensation based on Singapore product prices, while the ministry insists on production costs. The article notes the refiners' strong earnings and a July indictment over alleged price coordination (which they deny) weaken their case, and cites an analyst calling for an exit strategy from the cap.
opinion.why: 기름값 상한제의 비용을 결국 누가 부담하는지, 정부와 정유사가 손실 보상액을 두고 왜 맞서는지를 알면 가격 통제의 숨은 대가를 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: Seeing who ultimately pays for the fuel price cap, and why the government and refiners are fighting over compensation, reveals the hidden costs of price controls.

rows.title: France and Germany near deal on De Cos for ECB top job as EU confirms two candidates
rows.original_source: Euronews (Quirino Mealha), citing an EU official, El País and Handelsblatt
rows.summary: An EU official confirmed on Nov 13, during an informal EU leaders' summit in Dublin, that two candidates are in the running to replace Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president: Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, now head of the Bank for International Settlements, and Klaas Knot, former head of the Dutch central bank. Lagarde is leaving early, on 7 February 2027. Spain's El País reports that France and Germany are close to a package deal favouring De Cos, with Germany taking the ECB chief economist post and France the market operations seat Isabel Schnabel is vacating. Half of the ECB's six-member Executive Board is due to leave within about five months. Whoever is chosen will help set interest rates for the 20-country eurozone, affecting inflation, borrowing costs and the finances of heavily indebted states such as France.
rows.fact: An EU official confirmed two nominations for ECB president, which Euronews identifies as De Cos and Knot. German Chancellor Merz said an agreement was in sight but not final, with Berlin planning to present its proposal next week. Nominations for the two other open board seats close on Nov 18.
rows.outlook: Berlin expects a deal on the ECB posts by the end of the year, and European Council President António Costa aims to start formal consultations at the Nov 26 EU summit.
rows.why: 한 사람의 중앙은행 총재 선택이 20개국의 금리와 물가에 영향을 준다는 점에서, 통화정책이 정치적 협상과 어떻게 얽혀 있는지 이해할 수 있는 좋은 사례이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how choosing one central banker, which affects interest rates and prices in 20 countries, is tangled up in political bargaining between governments.
rows.term_def: The principle that a central bank sets interest rates on economic grounds, free from pressure by governments or politicians.
rows.note: Last-24h EU leadership decision (official confirmation of ECB candidates, Euronews Nov 13 17:35 GMT). No major European data release in the window. Body read in full; candidate field and Lagarde's Feb 7, 2027 exit cross-checked with Brussels Signal (Nov 9).

opinion.title: Why is ECB President Lagarde stepping down?
opinion.author: eurotopics editors (compiling Süddeutsche Zeitung, FAZ, Corriere della Sera, Les Echos, El País, Naftemporiki)
opinion.summary: This round-up gathers editorials from major European newspapers on Lagarde's early exit and the race to replace her. Süddeutsche Zeitung argues that leaving early lets her successor be chosen before France's spring 2027 election, so a possible far-right president would have no say, while Corriere della Sera sees a Paris-Berlin deal on several top jobs taking shape. Frankfurter Allgemeine wants a fiercely independent successor who insists on budget discipline, and Les Echos urges France to keep its influence. El País names Knot and De Cos as frontrunners while criticising a board that will have no women.
opinion.why: 같은 사건을 두고 독일·프랑스·이탈리아·스페인 언론이 자국의 이해관계에 따라 얼마나 다르게 해석하는지 비교하며 비판적으로 읽는 연습을 할 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: Comparing how German, French, Italian and Spanish papers read the same event through their own national interests is good practice in critical reading.

rows.title: Energy prices pushed exports, imports to record highs in October
rows.original_source: Business Standard (Krity Ambey), based on Ministry of Commerce and Industry data
rows.summary: India's goods exports reached a record $49.47 billion in October 2026, up about 45% from a year earlier, while goods imports hit a record $89.35 billion, widening the merchandise trade deficit to $39.88 billion, the largest in 12 months. High crude prices linked to the Middle East conflict, with the Indian crude basket averaging nearly $120 a barrel, lifted crude imports 54% to $22.82 billion and also raised the value of India's refined-fuel exports. Pre-Diwali gold buying and electronics imports added to the import bill. Services exports of about $40.5 billion produced a surplus of roughly $20 billion, offsetting about half of the goods gap. The data show how an oil-importing economy's trade balance and currency are exposed to global energy prices even while its exports grow fast.
rows.fact: Government data released on Nov 13 show record monthly goods exports ($49.47bn) and imports ($89.35bn) for October and a 12-month-high merchandise deficit of $39.88bn. Crude oil imports rose 54% year on year, and exports to the US, India's top market, rose about 39% to $8.72bn.
rows.outlook: ICRA's Aditi Nayar expects the FY27 current account deficit to stay modest at about 0.9% of GDP, with risks tilted upward.
rows.why: 수출이 사상 최대인데도 유가 때문에 무역적자가 커질 수 있다는 점을 통해, 에너지 수입국 경제가 국제 원자재 가격에 얼마나 민감한지 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows that even record exports can come with a widening trade deficit when oil prices are high, revealing how sensitive an energy-importing economy is to global commodity prices.
rows.term_def: The gap when a country spends more on buying goods from abroad (imports) than it earns from selling goods abroad (exports) in a given period.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: official India trade data released Nov 13 ~15:30 IST, before the 24h window; no last-24h Asian policy/data release found (China activity data and Japan Q3 GDP due Nov 16). Figures cross-checked against Reuters (via Investing.com, Business Recorder) and IANS.

opinion.title: India's $40 billion trade deficit raises concerns, but Axis Bank sees limited pressure on rupee. Here's why
opinion.author: Business Today Desk (reporting an Axis Bank Research note)
opinion.summary: Axis Bank Research says October's jump in the trade deficit is mostly seasonal, blaming delayed festive demand and noting gold accounts for about half of the roughly $10 billion rise from September. The note argues that strong services earnings and remittances, renewed foreign equity buying and easing oil prices should limit pressure on the rupee. It expects the current account deficit to stay near 1% of GDP in FY27. It also warns that a stronger dollar on US inflation and Fed-tightening expectations could still weigh on emerging-market currencies.
opinion.why: 무역적자라는 숫자 하나만 보고 판단하지 않고 서비스 수지·자본 유입·환율까지 함께 보는 경제 분석의 방법을 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches students to look beyond a single headline deficit number and weigh services trade, capital flows and the exchange rate together.
